output.brief:
Cancelling RotaWeave probably won't fix this. The decline is concentrated at Dock Street and Westgate. Both sites got the app in April and lost their coordinator on 1 May. Millbrook has the app but kept its coordinator, and it is steady (118 to 111). Quarry Lane lost its coordinator but never went live on the app, and it is also steady (86 to 80). So neither change alone explains the fall. The combination does.

The mechanism is visible in the booking records. The basic app tier has no recurring bookings, so regulars only keep their usual slot if staff book them before the Thursday release. Staff did this for about 74 bookings a week until April. Since May it has been about 3 a week, and an admin seat sits unused. At Dock Street and Westgate, 88% of regulars who lost their slot at least twice are now inactive, against 11% of those who kept it. Callbacks mostly cite "nobody booked me".

Background-check renewal and Commonplate don't explain it. 121 of the 123 who lapsed held a current check, and only 2 of 61 callbacks mentioned joining another group.

Next steps: have staff or a trained lead volunteer book regulars into their usual slots at Dock Street and Westgate, and phone lapsed regulars to offer the slot back. Review after 60 days. Keep the renewal requirement. Don't purge the roster. Confidence is fairly high. The main gap is that the evidence is observational.
